auth.mediaDescription: Midnight at a neon-western bar in FizzDragon City — the Mayor watches the lights still moving on his badge.
auth.mediaPrompt:
[Technical foundation] 4K UHD, 24fps, 2.35:1 widescreen, dark tones, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain.

[Scene: Late-night western cyber-bar]
Location: An old western saloon halfway up the volcano in FizzDragon City. Through the window, a flowing magma river and the distant neon silhouette of the city.
Interior:
- The bar counter is made of lava glass; magma flows slowly underneath
- The bartender is a mechanical octopus in a vest, mixing drinks and polishing glasses with all eight tentacles at once
- All lighting comes from neon tubes and floating holographic lanterns

[Ensemble of avatars (Zootopia × cyber-cowboy)]
Sweeping clockwise across the bar, every patron is a "too-cool" virtual avatar:
1. Corner 1: A white rabbit DJ in a fringed leather cape, two micro-holographic projectors hanging from her ears, mixing tracks with hand gestures.
2. Corner 2: A buffalo sheriff with metal mechanical legs and a cowboy vest, holographic badge flickering on his chest, head resting on the bar with a glowing blue drink in front of him.
3. By the bar: A fox that looks a lot like Nick from Zootopia — but more cybered out: ring-shaped data streams in his irises, glowing circuit patterns stitched into his jacket.
4. The other side of the bar: A nearly translucent holographic jellyfish-person wearing a cowboy hat, rolling an electronic cigar with a tentacle.

[Main action (Mayor Boar's late hour)]
Mayor Boar sits at the deepest end of the bar, hat brim pulled low, an untouched drink in front of him.
He looks down at the holographic badge on his chest, which projects a miniature map of FizzDragon City with light-points flowing across it.
He lifts his eyes to take in the lively yet calm crowd, a faint smile at the corner of his mouth, then pulls his hat brim back down.

[Style anchors]
Character aesthetic = Disney Zootopia expressiveness + the grit of a Western + the visual collision of cyberpunk
Environment = the cantina from Star Wars Tatooine + the back-alley atmosphere of Cyberpunk's city

Duration: 12 seconds.

whatIs.a: A platform for storytellers — three things in one. (1) An AI studio that drafts, storyboards, voices, and renders your work. (2) A crew network where writers, artists, and voice talent meet to ship projects together. (3) An IP Plaza where finished stories find their audience and backers.

howCrewWorks.q: How does the AI crew actually work?
howCrewWorks.a: A supervisor agent reads your project and routes each ask to the right specialist — Outliner, Episode Planner, Scriptwriter, Storyboard Designer, Art Director, and more. They share a project bible so characters, scenes, and props stay consistent across episodes.

howLong.q: How long does it take to make something?
howLong.a: About five minutes from idea to first frame. A single 60-second short typically renders in under fifteen minutes; a multi-episode arc can be planned and storyboarded in an afternoon.

styles.a: 437+ and growing — anime, cinematic, watercolor, 3D Pixar, comic, noir, pixel art, vaporwave, and more. The same script can be rendered in any style without rewriting a single line.

pricing.a: Free to start. Each phase has a clear, predictable credit cost shown up-front — no surprise bills mid-render. Heavier renders (long-form video, lip sync) consume more credits; planning and scripting are nearly free.

ownership.q: Do I own what I create?
ownership.a: Yes. You retain rights to your scripts, storyboards, and final renders. Commercial use is allowed on paid plans.

languages.q: What languages can I create in?
languages.a: Scripts and dialogue support English, 简体中文, and 繁體中文 today. Voice synthesis covers the same set with native-quality TTS, and more languages are on the roadmap.
